title: Spectral Uniformity Below the Inverse
summary: The inverse is the comparison point; it remains open whether any function can improve its spectral uniformity, with power permutations as a more approachable special case.

formal_statement.body: $\exists F\colon\mathbb F_{2^n}\to\mathbb F_{2^n}$: $\sigma(F)<\sigma(x\mapsto x^{-1})$, or prove that no such $F$ exists; special case: power permutations.

scope.domain: Structural questions about spectral uniformity of finite-field functions, with power permutations as a special family.
parameters: n: determines the finite-field domain and codomain size
spectral uniformity: comparison measure for the functions
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether any such function exists or prove that none exists; the more approachable special case is to resolve the same question for power permutations.

citations.label: Pairwise independence of AES-like block ciphers

progress.summary: The source presents this as an interesting open problem involving either a function with lower spectral uniformity than the inverse or a proof of nonexistence. It describes the power-permutation version as a more approachable special case and notes that the general nonexistence problem appears difficult.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., Pairwise independence of AES-like block ciphers
